name: Callirhoe

project_scope.selection_mode: Four already installed canonical species; genus lesson backfill only
project_scope.source_pool: Genus Study Index row 68; existing species records in content/taxa/Malvaceae/Callirhoe

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Turn a flower bud sideways and LOOK DIRECTLY BELOW THE CALYX. Are there three extra bractlets (an involucel/epicalyx)? If yes in this four-taxon set, the winecup branch is favored. If none, check whether the plant is annual or perennial and examine mature mericarps, stipules, leaf lobes and raceme versus panicle.
shared_traits: Mallow flowers with five petals and many stamens fused into a staminal column around the style; alternate stipulate leaves.
Leaves can be deeply palmately lobed, but leaf division alone does not reliably split the erect species.
Dry segmented schizocarps composed of individual mericarps; mericarp dehiscence, beaks and collar shape are highly informative.
Presence/absence of involucellar bractlets, bud calyx behavior and fruit architecture provide more confidence than flower color.
shared_genus_recognition.visual_glossary: The involucel is an extra ring of typically three small bracts outside and just beneath the true five-lobed calyx; it is NOT a sixth sepal or a petal.

species_comparison_matrix.Callirhoe involucrata: 3 present, easily seen on intact bud (occasionally flattened against sepals)
Divergent in bud, NOT forming a pointed apex
Perennial, often spreading/decumbent with low stems
species_comparison_matrix.Callirhoe digitata: Tall erect perennial from thickened root
species_comparison_matrix.Callirhoe leiocarpa: Annual or sometimes biennial, erect to weakly erect
species_comparison_matrix.Callirhoe pedata: Erect or weakly erect perennial with storage taproot
species_comparison_matrix.weight: IMPORTANT second branch; verify root/life history safely

species_comparison_matrix.Callirhoe involucrata: Racemose; persistent ovate to ovate-lanceolate stipules

species_comparison_matrix.character: mature mericarp openings, beaks and collars
species_comparison_matrix.Callirhoe involucrata: Usually indehiscent with weak/nonprominent beaks; 2-lobed collar
species_comparison_matrix.Callirhoe leiocarpa: Dehiscent, conspicuous beaks ca. 1–2 mm and well-developed 3-lobed collars
species_comparison_matrix.Callirhoe pedata: Indehiscent, beaks variable; collar absent or weakly developed

look_here_first_sequence.structure: flower bud side view, both calyx and just-below-calyx region
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Three distinct involucellar bractlets + divergent calyx lobes → C. involucrata branch. Confirm trailing perennial habit.

look_here_first_sequence.structure: stem/root and ripe mericarps if involucel absent
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Annual/biennial and mericarps with prominent beaks, 3-lobed collars and dehiscence → C. leiocarpa branch. Immature fruit is not enough.

look_here_first_sequence.structure: stipules, branching arrangement of flower stalks and fully expanded leaves
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Tall erect perennial, caducous stipules, paniculate flowering and more numerous narrow leaf lobes → C. digitata candidate, subject to nonlocal-range caution.

look_here_first_sequence.structure: stem nodes, inflorescence and mature fruit
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Perennial, persistent narrow stipules, racemose inflorescence and 3–5-lobed foliage → C. pedata candidate.

look_here_first_sequence.structure: conflicting characters or absent bud/mature fruit
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Record Callirhoe sp.; photograph involucel, stipules, habit and fruit instead of guessing from a pink/purple cup-shaped flower.

overlap_and_cautions: C. digitata is retained as a comparison/teaching concept: existing canonical species record notes current Kew/FNA ranges place true C. digitata outside Texas. Do NOT infer project-target nativity from its presence in this module.
C. pedata and C. digitata have both been confused in historical literature, including the name C. digitata var. stipulata; accepted-concept mapping belongs to taxonomy lane.
C. leiocarpa has historical misidentifications as C. pedata; mature dehiscent mericarps and annual habit are safer than petal color.
C. involucrata is variable at variety level; do not force an infraspecific ID from flower shade.
Involucel bractlets can lie flat against sepals, especially in open flowers; check unopened buds and take a lateral close-up.
Leaf lobes and stem height overlap across species and mowing may affect habit; preserve juvenile-versus-adult context.
Do not handle rare/nonlocal comparison taxa as locally confirmed natives without independent county evidence. Species range labels already in the canonical records are unchanged.

local_lookalike_routing.taxon: Callirhoe scabriuscula (regional genus comparison, not canonical here)
local_lookalike_routing.separator: Erect and densely stellate-hairy; inspect involucel and fruit rather than assuming any tall winecup is C. pedata or C. leiocarpa.
Confirm number and arrangement of involucellar bracts, calyx, staminal column, leaf shape and mature schizocarp mericarps; some have superficially mallow-like flowers and hairy foliage.

local_lookalike_routing.taxon: Hibiscus spp. and other large-flowered mallows
local_lookalike_routing.separator: Show fruit and calyx/epicalyx detail: Hibiscus often has a true capsule rather than Callirhoe's dry mericarp ring; color alone is misleading.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.role: same-scale ripe mericarp close-ups, dorsal and lateral
diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: dehiscent vs indehiscent, beak and 3-lobed vs weak/2-lobed collar; ruler
caducous vs persistent narrow vs persistent auriculate stipules; panicle vs raceme
trailing vs erect, annual vs perennial context, 3–5 vs 5–10 lobes; note growth stage
open dehiscent mericarp vs closed indehiscent mericarp; do not use immature fruit
five petals, fused staminal column, calyx, involucel, ovary to schizocarp sequence
